results.title: Fenner’s eight steers Demons to grand final
results.description: Laharum’s senior football side will play in the 2026 Horsham District Football Netball League grand final after defeating Noradjuha Quantong in the second semi-final on Saturday August 29. In warm conditions at Rupanyup, the Demons kicked 10.9 (69) to the Bombers' 7.9 (51), led by eight goals by Jack Fenner. Noradjuha Quantong struck immediately on the first bounce, scoring through Dyson Parish in the opening half-minute of the game. Some forward momentum eventually led to Jack Fenner's first goal, but a major to Declan Phyland later in the quarter ensured the Bombers led 14-9 at the first break. The Bombers won the territory and possession battle for most of the second quarter; however, two Fenner goals late in the half helped the Demons edge ahead 23-22 by half-time. Some swift possessions upfield led to two Bombers goals early in the second half, but the momentum was quickly quashed by a Reuben Launder goal stemming from a 50-metre penalty. Some good execution in the midfield and forward line late in the quarter resulted in three goals by Fenner, helping Laharum to a 48-43 lead at the final break. The Demons continued to capitalise upfield, extending their lead to four goals midway through the final term. Despite continual forward pressure from the Bombers, Laharum continued to repel Noradjuha Quantong, holding on to win by 18 points. Along with Fenner's eight-goal performance, Todd Heynen and Patrick MacDonough were strong in the backline for the Demons, while Shannon Argall and Daniel Easson impressed in the midfield. For Noradjuha Quantong, Brock Orval finished with three goals, while Jack Vague, Lee Dale, Tom Netherway, Declan Phyland and Brandon Ellis were among the side's best in the loss. Laharum coach Robbie Miller said he was very happy to make it to the decider but added the job was not done yet. "It feels good but we also know that there is an opportunity in front of us now," Miller said. "We're enjoying this moment and then we we'll get back to work straight away. "We know it's a tough contest, whoever we come up against. "We got ourselves there; hopefully we can replicate that type of football and get the win in a fortnight." Asked about their second-half performance, the Laharum coach said his side did a better job of winning the ball around the contest. "Noradjuha Quantong have some great ball winners and ball users and they were beating us to the ball, particularly around the stoppage and in clearances," Miller said. "Once we knuckled down in that area, the quicker ball movement into our forward 50 and isolating our forwards a bit more worked rather than allowing them time to get back on the defensive end. "It was a combination of a few things, but it's good to know that when the going is tough we can still grind out those types of wins and that our game plan comes through." With the side creating plenty of opportunities for Fenner in the forward line, Miller said he was pleased with the growing improvement of the team in the half-forward area. "We've worked so hard during the week on our forward line functioning a little bit better and presenting up at the ball and not getting in each other's leading lanes," he said. "I think today we showed glimpses, but there's still room for improvement."

results.title: Summit Point returns to PGT spotlight, ready to test Tour’s best
results.description: Nine years after last hosting a Philippine Golf Tour championship, Summit Point Golf and Country Club makes a much-anticipated return to the PGT calendar, ready to once again put the country’s top professionals through one of the tour’s most demanding tests. The ICTSI Summit Point Championship blasts off Sept. 8-11 in Lipa City, Batangas, with the Robert Trent Jones II-designed layout expected to challenge the men and ladies of the PGT with its combination of length, strategy and precision. Clyde Mondilla ruled the last PGT event staged at Summit Point – the ICTSI Players Championship – and went on to capture the 2017 PGT Order of Merit crown. Now, nearly a decade later, the course returns to the spotlight with another strong field eager to make its mark on a layout that rewards aggression off the tee but demands discipline from start to finish. Known as the country’s first “tribute” course, Summit Point features holes modeled after renowned layouts and signature holes from famous international courses. But while its design pays homage to golf landmarks around the world, it has developed a character and set of challenges all its own. At 7,017 yards, the course gives the long hitters plenty of opportunities to attack, but power alone will not be enough to conquer it. Recent monsoon rains have softened the fairways, potentially narrowing the advantage of the biggest hitters. Strong winds are also expected to add another layer of difficulty. The mix of short, strategic holes and long, demanding par-4s and par-5s will require players to make sound decisions throughout the four rounds. Large bunkers, water hazards and ravines stand ready to punish errant shots, while precise approach play and a dependable short game could prove decisive. The four par-3s could also emerge as pivotal holes in the championship. With little room for error, they offer opportunities to gain ground – or quickly derail a title bid. Reigning Order of Merit champion Angelo Que and Mondilla are expected to banner the field in the P2.5 million championship, the fifth leg of the 10-stage circuit organized by Pilipinas Golf Tournaments, Inc. The event comes after a lengthy two-month break in the PGT calendar, with the last two legs played in July. Lloyd Go swept those final two stops, prevailing in contrasting fashion at the tight, undulating Pinewoods course in Baguio before edging Tony Lascuña by one stroke at the flat and wide Pradera Verde in Pampanga. The extended break should leave the field both rested and hungry, giving the pros – including those competing in the accompanying 54-hole, P1 million Ladies PGT – more time to sharpen their games and prepare for the second half of the season. Several players have also seen action in overseas tournaments during the hiatus, adding another intriguing element to the battle at Summit Point. But much of the attention will inevitably center on the course itself. Summit Point's return to the PGT stage provides a distinctly different challenge from the tour's recent stops. It invites players to unleash their power, yet punishes indiscriminate aggression. The softened fairways could encourage more attacking lines, but the hazards, ravines and demanding approach shots will require players to know when to push and when to play conservatively. After nine years away, Summit Point is back – and it is poised to make the PGT's return a test of not just who can hit it farthest, but who can manage the course, withstand the conditions and remain patient over four demanding days.
